{{Short description|Italian mathematician (1891–1958)}}
'''Francesco Sbrana''' (10 June 1891, [[Portoferraio]], [[Elba]] – 23 October 1958, Genoa) was an Italian applied mathematician and mathematical physicist.<ref name=Bio>{{cite web|title=Francesco Sbrana (1891 – 1958|website=Edizione Nazionale Mathematica Italiana, mathematica.sns.it|url=http://mathematica.sns.it/autori/1224/}}</ref>

Sbrana received in 1914 his ''laurea'' from the [[University of Genova]], where he became an assistant in rational mechanics to [[Orazio Tedone]]. After Tedone's death in 1922, Sbrana taught the academic courses formerly taught by Tedone and in 1931 became the successor to the professorial chair of rational mechanics, where he continued until his death in 1958. Sbrana did research in mathematical analysis, geometry, and especially rational mechanics and mathematical physics,<ref name=Bio/> including the theory of perfect fluids,<ref>Sbrana, Francesco. Sulla validità del teorema di Bernoulli per un fluido reale. Coop. tipografica Azzoguidi, 1931.</ref> elastic deformations,<ref>Sbrana, Francesco, and Mario Bossolasco. "Sul regime termico degli strati superiori della crosta terrestre." Pure and Applied Geophysics 23, no. 1 (1952): 21–26.</ref> and the ''metodo simbolico'' introduced by [[Giovanni Giorgi]].<ref>Sbrana, F. "Sull’equazione caratteristica dei problemi di propagazione in una dimensione." Rendiconti del Circolo Matematico di Palermo (1884–1940) 56, no. 1 (1932): 58–64. {{doi|10.1007/BF03017708}}</ref><ref>Sbrana, Francesco. "Sopra un gruppo di operatori funzionali che interessano la Fisica." Annali di Matematica Pura ed Applicata 7, no. 1 (1929): 33–45. {{doi|10.1007/BF02409967}}</ref>

Sbrana was an Invited Speaker of the [[International Congress of Mathematicians|ICM]] in 1928 in Bologna.
